questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Corona texture, manifesting as reaction rims around minerals, results from which metamorphic process?
options: Incomplete reaction during cooling — mineral replacement textures (e.g., olivine rimmed by orthopyroxene + spinel in granulites)
Complete equilibrium melting of the protolith producing a homogeneous melt
Eutectic crystallization of melt into cumulate layers without post-cumulus reaction
Mechanical mixing of layers during sedimentary transport forming graded units
questions.solution: Incomplete reaction during cooling — mineral replacement textures (e.g., olivine rimmed by orthopyroxene + spinel in granulites)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which term describes the flat, gently sloping surface cut by wave erosion at the base of a sea cliff?
options: Sea cliff — steep vertical face retreating landward under wave attack
Beach — depositional feature formed by sediment accumulation
Marine terrace — uplifted former wave-cut platform now above sea level

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Normal MORB (N-MORB) derives from a depleted mantle source, evidenced by what light REE pattern and (La/Sm)ₙ value?
options: Light REE depleted pattern with (La/Sm)ₙ < 1, reflecting ~6–8% partial melting of spinel lherzolite
Light REE enriched pattern with (La/Sm)ₙ > 1 from an enriched mantle source
Flat REE pattern with (La/Sm)ₙ ≈ 1 from a primitive mantle source
Strong positive Nb anomaly with high ³He/⁴He from a plume-derived source
questions.solution: Light REE depleted pattern with (La/Sm)ₙ < 1, reflecting ~6–8% partial melting of spinel lherzolite

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the water-table fluctuation (WTF) method, groundwater recharge is estimated using which relationship?
options: Recharge = S_y × (dH/dt) + discharge, where S_y is specific yield and dH/dt is water-table rise rate
Drawdown analysis using the Theis equation for aquifer parameter estimation
Steady-state Thiem equation applied to two observation wells
Pumping test recovery data matched to type curves for transmissivity
questions.solution: Recharge = S_y × (dH/dt) + discharge, where S_y is specific yield and dH/dt is water-table rise rate

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Radiocarbon (¹⁴C) dating applies to organic material up to what maximum age, and what key requirement does it have?
options: < 50 ka; requires calibration against tree-ring, coral, or speleothem records
< 100 ka; requires no calibration as decay is constant
< 10 ka; requires U-Pb zircon dating for verification
< 1 Ma; requires Rb-Sr whole-rock isochron for correction
questions.solution: < 50 ka; requires calibration against tree-ring, coral, or speleothem records

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Geotechnical investigation borehole spacing primarily depends on:
options: Site complexity and size/type of the proposed structure
Only the overall height of the proposed structure
Only the financial budget allocated for the investigation
No standard exists; spacing is entirely at the driller's discretion
questions.solution: Site complexity and size/type of the proposed structure

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Seismic P-wave velocity in rocks generally increases with:
options: Increasing elastic modulus and increasing density (with modulus dominating)
Increasing porosity saturated with low-density fluids
Decreasing temperature and increasing pore pressure
Decreasing density while shear modulus remains constant
questions.solution: Increasing elastic modulus and increasing density (with modulus dominating)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The dip direction of cross-bedding foresets in a sandstone indicates:
options: Paleocurrent direction (flow direction at time of deposition)
Paleo-water depth at the depositional site
Provenance area of the detrital sediment
Relative age of the sedimentary unit
questions.solution: Paleocurrent direction (flow direction at time of deposition)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The meteoric phreatic diagenetic environment is characterized by:
options: Freshwater-saturated zone below the water table; equant calcite cement, common dissolution, δ¹⁸O-depleted isotopes
Vadose zone above water table; meniscus and pendant cements, gravitational cements
Marine phreatic zone; aragonite needle cements, micrite envelopes, Mg-calcite
Deep burial zone; pressure dissolution, stylolites, ferroan calcite, quartz cement
questions.solution: Freshwater-saturated zone below the water table; equant calcite cement, common dissolution, δ¹⁸O-depleted isotopes

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Stretching lineation in metamorphic rocks indicates:
options: Direction of maximum stretching (finite strain axis X)
Trace of the fold axial plane on the foliation
Dip direction of the dominant fault plane
questions.solution: Direction of maximum stretching (finite strain axis X)

Eclogite facies: > 2.7 GPa, 600–800 °C; omphacite + garnet ± coesite
Greenschist facies: < 0.5 GPa, 300–450 °C; chlorite + actinolite + albite
questions.solution: > 900 °C at 7–13 kbar; diagnostic assemblages include sapphirine + quartz, orthopyroxene + sillimanite, osumilite

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Object-based image analysis (OBIA) differs from pixel-based classification by:
options: First segmenting the image into objects, then classifying segments using spectral, shape, texture, and contextual features
Classifying each pixel independently using only spectral values (maximum likelihood)
Applying band-ratio indices to the entire image without segmentation
Using unsupervised clustering (ISODATA) on pixel spectra alone
questions.solution: First segmenting the image into objects, then classifying segments using spectral, shape, texture, and contextual features

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A Type 1 sequence boundary differs from a Type 2 sequence boundary in that:
options: Type 1: shelf exposed (base level falls below shelf edge); Type 2: shelf not exposed (base level falls but remains above shelf edge)
Type 1 forms during transgression; Type 2 forms during regression
Type 1 is a conformable surface; Type 2 is an unconformity
Type 1 correlates with maximum flooding surface; Type 2 correlates with transgressive surface
questions.solution: Type 1: shelf exposed (base level falls below shelf edge); Type 2: shelf not exposed (base level falls but remains above shelf edge)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Gneiss, a high-grade metamorphic rock, is characteristically identified by:
options: Compositional banding (gneissic foliation) — segregation of light and dark mineral layers
Schistosity — planar alignment of platy minerals (e.g., mica)
Slaty cleavage — fine-grained fissility from clay mineral alignment
Mylonitic foliation — extreme grain-size reduction in fault zones
questions.solution: Compositional banding (gneissic foliation) — segregation of light and dark mineral layers

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An accretionary wedge (accretionary prism) consists of:

Ophiolite suite — obducted oceanic crust and upper mantle
High-grade metamorphic core complex — exhumed deep crustal rocks
Volcanic arc — magmatic rocks from flux melting above the slab
questions.solution: Thrust-faulted, folded sedimentary rocks and mélanges (blocks in matrix) scraped off the subducting plate

questions.solution: Matrix-supported, poorly sorted, angular clasts, lacking grading or stratification

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The extinction angle of a mineral in thin section under crossed polars is defined as:

The angle between the two optic axes (2V angle)
The angle between the polarizer and analyzer (always 90°)
The angle between the stage rotation and the mineral's optic axis
questions.solution: The angle between a crystallographic direction (cleavage trace or long axis) and the nearest vibration direction at extinction

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic rocks form by the action of which agents on pre-existing rocks?

questions.solution: Heat and/or pressure (and chemically active fluids) in the solid state

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Calcareous nannofossils (coccoliths), typically < 30 µm and ranging from Cretaceous to Recent, are primarily used for:

Deep-sea paleoceanography using radiolarian silica tests
questions.solution: High-resolution biostratigraphy and paleoclimate reconstruction (e.g., Emiliania huxleyi as a paleotemperature proxy)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The primary factors controlling metamorphic mineral assemblages and textures are:

Fluid pressure and strain rate only
questions.solution: Temperature, pressure, fluid composition (H₂O, CO₂), time, and protolith chemical composition

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Tsunamis are most commonly generated by, and typically require thrust-fault earthquakes of what minimum magnitude:

Gravitational pull of Moon and Sun (tides, not tsunamis)
Wind-driven surface currents and storms (storm surge, not tsunami)
Submarine landslides only (can generate tsunamis but less common than earthquakes)
questions.solution: Submarine thrust-fault earthquakes of M > 7; long wavelength (> 100 km), velocity ≈ √(gh)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In geostatistics, kriging interpolation is best described as:
options: Best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) using the variogram to weight neighboring samples, minimizing estimation variance
Inverse distance weighting (IDW) — weights by distance only, no variogram
Nearest neighbor (polygonal) — assigns nearest sample value to the block
Simple arithmetic average of all samples within the search radius
questions.solution: Best linear unbiased estimator (BLUE) using the variogram to weight neighboring samples, minimizing estimation variance

options: Low sulfidation (quartz–adularia–sericite, Au–Ag) and high sulfidation (quartz–alunite–kaolinite, enargite–Au)
Porphyry Cu–Au (potassic) and skarn (calc-silicate) — porphyry-related, not epithermal
VHMS (Cu–Zn) and SEDEX (Pb–Zn) — submarine exhalative, not epithermal
Orogenic Au (quartz–carbonate) and Carlin-type (decalcification) — structurally controlled, not epithermal
questions.solution: Low sulfidation (quartz–adularia–sericite, Au–Ag) and high sulfidation (quartz–alunite–kaolinite, enargite–Au)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Coalbed methane (CBM) is stored in coal primarily by which mechanism, and how is it recovered?
options: Methane adsorbed on coal matrix surfaces; recovered by dewatering to reduce pressure and induce desorption
Free gas in cleats and fractures; recovered by hydraulic fracturing alone
Dissolved in formation water; recovered by pumping water and gas together
Trapped in micropores as compressed gas; recovered by CO₂ injection (ECBM)
questions.solution: Methane adsorbed on coal matrix surfaces; recovered by dewatering to reduce pressure and induce desorption

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS) deposits, formed by submarine hydrothermal exhalative activity, are enriched in:
options: Cu–Zn–Pb ± Au–Ag, with associated Fe, As, Sb; stratiform lenses over stringer feeder zones
Ni–Co–Pt (lateritic or magmatic sulfide, not VMS)
questions.solution: Cu–Zn–Pb ± Au–Ag, with associated Fe, As, Sb; stratiform lenses over stringer feeder zones

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 25% of its original parent isotope (half-life = 1.3 Gyr). Its radiometric age is approximately:
options: 1.3 Gyr (one half-life, confusing fraction with age)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: On a block diagram, an inclined bedding plane dips at 30°. The dip direction is, by definition:
options: Perpendicular to the strike, in the direction of steepest descent of the plane
Parallel to the strike (this is the strike direction, not dip)
Vertical downward (confusing dip angle with dip direction)
Horizontal along the strike (confusing strike line with dip direction)
questions.solution: Perpendicular to the strike, in the direction of steepest descent of the plane

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The hypsometric curve plots, and its shape indicates basin erosion stage by:
options: Relative area vs. relative elevation; youthful = convex (high integral >0.6), mature = S-shaped, old = concave (low integral <0.3)
River channel length vs. elevation (longitudinal profile, not hypsometry)
Valley width vs. downstream distance (cross-valley profile)
Discharge vs. time at a gauging station (hydrograph)
questions.solution: Relative area vs. relative elevation; youthful = convex (high integral >0.6), mature = S-shaped, old = concave (low integral <0.3)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Supervised image classification differs from unsupervised classification by:
options: Using analyst-defined training samples of known classes to classify all remaining pixels
Clustering pixels into spectral groups without any training data (unsupervised)
Applying fixed spectral thresholds to assign classes (density slicing)
Manually digitizing boundaries by visual interpretation (photointerpretation)
questions.solution: Using analyst-defined training samples of known classes to classify all remaining pixels

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Earthquake magnitude and intensity differ in that:
options: Magnitude (Mw, Richter) measures energy released at the source; intensity (MMI) measures observed shaking and damage at a site
Magnitude measures damage; intensity measures energy (reversed)
Both are identical scales measuring the same quantity
Intensity is instrument-only; magnitude is visual-only (reversed)
questions.solution: Magnitude (Mw, Richter) measures energy released at the source; intensity (MMI) measures observed shaking and damage at a site

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Bowen's discontinuous reaction series (mafic branch) crystallizes in the order:
options: Olivine → pyroxene → amphibole → biotite (increasing SiO₂, decreasing temperature)
All crystallize simultaneously at a single temperature
questions.solution: Olivine → pyroxene → amphibole → biotite (increasing SiO₂, decreasing temperature)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Siwalik Group (molasse of the Himalayan foreland) is subdivided into:
options: Lower (Kamliyal/Chinji), Middle (Nagri, Dhok Pathan), Upper (Tatrot, Pinjor, Boulder Conglomerate)
Two divisions: marine shelf and deltaic (oversimplified)
Five divisions based solely on conglomerate grain size (not the standard scheme)
Four divisions of equal thickness from cyclic bedding (not recognized)
questions.solution: Lower (Kamliyal/Chinji), Middle (Nagri, Dhok Pathan), Upper (Tatrot, Pinjor, Boulder Conglomerate)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In carbonate diagenesis, neomorphism refers to:
options: Replacement of aragonite or high-Mg calcite by low-Mg calcite of different crystal size (aggrading neomorphism: microspar → pseudospar)
Replacement of calcite by dolomite in Mg-rich brines (dolomitization, not neomorphism)
Replacement of limestone by microcrystalline quartz (silicification)
Complete dissolution and reprecipitation as blocky calcite in pores (cementation, not neomorphism)
questions.solution: Replacement of aragonite or high-Mg calcite by low-Mg calcite of different crystal size (aggrading neomorphism: microspar → pseudospar)

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Contact (thermal) metamorphism is produced mainly by, and occurs where relative to an intrusion:
options: Heat from a magma intrusion; forms a contact aureole in the surrounding country rock
Regional pressure over an orogenic belt (regional metamorphism)
Shock waves from meteorite impact (shock metamorphism)
Hot seawater circulation at mid-ocean ridges (hydrothermal metamorphism)
questions.solution: Heat from a magma intrusion; forms a contact aureole in the surrounding country rock

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The fastest seismic body waves, which arrive first at a station, are:
questions.solution: P-waves are compressional and travel fastest, arriving before slower S and surface waves.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a variogram model, the sill and range represent which aspects of spatial variability?
options: Constant semivariance at all lags, implying no spatial correlation in the data
Semivariance vs distance. Sill = total variance. Range = correlation length
A linear semivariance increasing without bound, implying that no finite sill value exists
Semivariance that is undefined because the regionalized variable is purely random
questions.solution: Variogram: γ(h) = ½E[(Z(x)-Z(x+h))²]. Spherical, exponential, Gaussian models. Nugget effect.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does porosity typically differ between the core and the damage zone of a fault zone?
options: Core: low porosity (gouge). Damage zone: high fracture porosity. Conduit-barrier
The fault core is the most porous part and the damage zone acts as a sealing barrier to flow
Porosity increases steadily and monotonically from the protolith toward the fault core
The entire fault zone has uniform porosity equal to the undeformed host rock's porosity
questions.solution: Fault seal: clay smear, cataclasis. Juxtaposition seal. Membrane seal (capillary entry pressure).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which parameters are used to judge the quality of coal intended for coking?
options: Only the ash content of the raw coal as mined from the seam as it is produced
Moisture content and volatile matter alone in the as-received sample of the coal
Sulphur and phosphorus content of the coal as determined by ultimate analysis
Caking index (GRI), CRI (coke reactivity), CSR (coke strength after reaction)
questions.solution: Coking: GRI >70 for good coking. CRI <25, CSR >65 for blast furnace coke.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: U-shaped valleys, cirques, arêtes, horns, hanging valleys and moraines are landforms created by which agent?
options: Cone of sediment deposited where a mountain stream abruptly meets a plain at the foot of the mountain front
Narrow steep-sided valley produced by active river downcutting and vertical incision of the river bed
U-shaped valley, cirque, arête, horn, hanging valley, moraine (lateral, medial, terminal)
Sediment body deposited where a river enters a lake or sea and spreads out into the standing body of quiet water beyond
questions.solution: Glacial: erosion (U-valley) and deposition (moraine, drumlin, esker, till).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In GIS, landslide susceptibility mapping commonly uses a weighted overlay of which factors such as slope, geology, rainfall, and land use?
options: Analysis that uses a single factor only, such as the slope gradient being considered alone
Weighted overlay: slope, geology, rainfall, land use, distance to faults
The distance to rivers only, while ignoring the geology and land use factors entirely
Rainfall intensity that is recorded over just a single monsoon season period
questions.solution: Susceptibility: heuristic, statistical (logistic regression), deterministic (infinite slope). Machine learning.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Squeezing ground in a tunnel results from high stress acting on weak rock that deforms:
options: High stress in weak rock → plastic deformation. Invert struts needed
Rapid brittle failure of the rock mass with sudden and violent bursting
Continuous inflow of gas under high pressure from the tunnel face
High-permeability rock with steady seepage into the excavation
questions.solution: Squeezing: ductile deformation. Caused by high overburden, weak rock (shale).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Lamprophyre: volatile-rich, porphyritic mafic igneous rock. Phenocrysts typically:
options: Quartz and alkali feldspar set in a coarse-grained equigranular matrix
Amphibole, biotite, or olivine in fine groundmass
Only quartz phenocrysts in a groundmass free of ferromagnesian minerals
Plagioclase and sanidine phenocrysts in a glassy volcanic matrix
questions.solution: Lamprophyre: lamprophyric texture. Dark minerals as phenocrysts. Often associated with diamond pipes.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does the principle of original horizontality state about the deposition of sediments?
options: Sediments always deposited inclined at the angle of repose of the grains
Sediments deposited in curved and wavy surfaces following the basin contours
Sediments deposited in near-vertical sheets along active fault scarps
questions.solution: Steno: tilted beds indicate post-depositional deformation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The hornblende hornfels facies, a moderate-grade contact metamorphic facies, is characterized by which assemblage?
options: Contact metamorphism, moderate grade. Plagioclase + hornblende + cordierite
Low-grade contact metamorphism in which albite and epidote minerals remain stable
Regional metamorphism at high pressure typical of active subduction zones
Very high-grade contact metamorphism with pyroxene and no hydrous minerals remaining stable

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An ore body of 5 Mt has an average metal grade of 1%. The contained metal is about:
questions.solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 5 Mt × 1% = 50 thousand tonnes (kt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 19.5 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following measures is used to mitigate debris flows?
options: Contour bunding and terracing of the entire catchment area
Removing all vegetation to expose the source material
Check dams, deflection walls, sabo dams, early warning
Raising the channel bed with loose excavated spoil
questions.solution: Debris flow: high velocity mixture of soil, rock, water. Runout distance analysis.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does a mudstone differ from a shale in terms of fissility and bedding?
options: Lithified mud (silt + clay). Massive, no fissility
Coarse-grained rock of well-rounded quartz sand with cross-bedding
Fissile mudrock that splits easily along bedding planes into thin sheets
Volcanic rock with a glassy texture formed by rapid cooling of lava
questions.solution: Mudstone vs shale: shale splits into thin layers (fissile).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which matrix and statistics, including the Kappa coefficient, are used to assess how accurately an image has been classified?
options: Reporting only a single overall accuracy percentage, without any per-class detail whatsoever being provided to the analyst
A simple visual comparison of the classified map with the original source imagery
Confusion matrix. Overall accuracy, producer's accuracy, user's accuracy. Kappa coefficient
Simply accepting the classification results, without performing any formal validation step whatsoever
questions.solution: Confusion matrix: errors of omission (producer's) and commission (user's). Kappa: chance-corrected agreement.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geodetic technique can monitor crustal deformation with millimetre precision and track plate motion of a few centimetres per year?
options: Crustal deformation monitoring (mm precision). Plate motion ~cm/yr
Useful for navigation only, and is unsuitable for any scientific monitoring
Mapping of roads and property boundaries at the regional scales, nothing more
Photogrammetric mapping of the terrain, without using any ground-based receivers at all
questions.solution: GPS: continuous GPS stations. Earthquake cycle: interseismic, coseismic, postseismic deformation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does fault gouge thickness typically vary with fault displacement and depth?
options: Increases with displacement and decreases with depth
Decreases with displacement and increases with depth below the surface
Remains constant regardless of the amount of slip or the depth of burial
Increases with depth but is unaffected by the total accumulated displacement
questions.solution: Gouge thickness: t ∝ d^α (α≈0.5). Thicker at shallow depth (more brittle).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rhyolite vs granite: same composition but:
options: Both rocks share the same texture because cooling rates are identical
Rhyolite is mafic while granite is felsic in bulk composition
Rhyolite: volcanic (fine-grained or glassy). Granite: plutonic (coarse-grained)
They differ in composition, rhyolite being richer in quartz and poorer in alkali
questions.solution: Rhyolite: volcanic equivalent of granite. Same bulk composition. Texture differs due to cooling rate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The fold shown in cross-section (beds arch upward about the axial plane) is a(n):
questions.solution: Upward-arching limbs dipping away from the axis define an anticline (oldest beds in core).

questions.stem: In the Hvorslev method of slug test analysis, hydraulic conductivity K is estimated using:
options: K = r²·ln(L/R)/(2·L·T₀). T₀ = time for 37% recovery
K = Q/(2πT) for steady radial flow toward the pumping well
K = T/S from the ratio of transmissivity to storativity
K = Q·W(u)/s evaluated at the match point of a type curve
questions.solution: Hvorslev: for low-K formations. T₀ from semi-log plot of water level vs time.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A perched water table forms when a low-permeability lens creates:
options: Local saturated zone above region water table due to low-permeability lens
The regional water table surface that lies within a low permeability rock basin
An unsaturated interval lying directly beneath the regional water table
The piezometric surface of a deeply buried confined aquifer system
questions.solution: Perched: clay lens creates local saturation. Limited yield. Shallow wells.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The GASP geobarometer, sensitive to pressure, is based on which net-transfer reaction?
options: Fe-Mg exchange between garnet and biotite giving an independent temperature estimate for the same rock
Grossular + Al₂SiO₅ + Quartz → Anorthite. Pressure-sensitive. Used with Grt-Bt thermometer
Aluminum saturation index of the bulk rock used to infer crystallization depth of the source magma
Si-content of phengite calibrated as a temperature-dependent barometer for low-grade pelitic schists
questions.solution: GASP: Ca transfer. K = a_An³/(a_Grs·a_Ky²·a_Qz). P from equilibrium constant.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: For a geological cross-section to be considered balanced, what condition must be satisfied during restoration?
options: Conservation of bed length alone, ignoring any changes in the area of individual layers
Uniform horizontal shortening applied equally to every layer in the section without pinning
Conservation of bed length and area during restoration
Restoration with gap formation permitted in the synclines and fold crests of the section
questions.solution: Balanced: no gaps or overlaps after restoration. Bed length and area preserved.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Basalt is best classified as which kind of igneous rock based on its texture and composition?
options: Coarse-grained intrusive rock rich in quartz and alkali feldspar
Chemical sedimentary rock precipitated from a saturated brine solution
High-grade metamorphic rock showing distinct compositional banding
questions.solution: Basalt is the fine-grained, dark, mafic rock formed from rapidly cooled lava.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In deformed layered sequences, the sausage-like segmentation of competent beds known as boudinage indicates which strain condition?
options: Dextral shear across the rock mass
Strike-slip displacement along a fault plane
questions.solution: Boudinage: layer stretched and broken into sausage-shaped blocks. Indicates extension along layering. Common in metamorphic rocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The width of a wave-cut platform is controlled primarily by the combined influence of which factors?
options: The width is controlled only by the rate of sea-level change
The width is controlled only by the rock resistance
The width is controlled only by the wave energy at the coast
Rate of sea-level change, rock resistance, wave energy
questions.solution: Platform: wider in weak rock, high wave energy, stable sea level. Narrow: resistant rock, rapid sea-level change.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In sedimentary geology, what does the provenance of a sediment refer to?
options: The mechanism of sediment transport from source to the basin of deposition
Source area of sediments (composition, age, tectonic setting)
The environment in which sediments are deposited and later lithified into rock
Post-depositional changes including compaction, cementation and dissolution of sediment
questions.solution: Provenance: heavy mineral analysis, zircon U-Pb dating, paleocurrents.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the main advantage of Ar-Ar dating compared with the conventional K-Ar method?
options: Produces results much faster in the laboratory than the conventional K-Ar method on the same mineral separates
Single heating step or step heating for age spectrum. No need for separate K measurement
Considerably cheaper to run on bulk samples of the same rock that is being dated
More accurate ages for carbonate sediments and their cements in the section
questions.solution: Ar-Ar: irradiation converts ³⁹K to ³⁹Ar. Step heating: age spectrum. Plateau age = undisturbed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which logging techniques are used to determine in-situ rock properties in boreholes?
options: Gamma, resistivity, SP, caliper, sonic logging. In-situ rock properties
Only the measurement of core recovery and RQD from the recovered drill core
Only water level measurement in the borehole after completion
Geophysical profiling along the ground surface above the borehole
questions.solution: Well logging: lithology, porosity, density, water quality. Acoustic televiewer: fractures.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which geophysical method offers high resolution but limited shallow depth penetration?
options: Ground penetrating radar. High resolution, shallow (<10m)
Electromagnetic sounding for deep crustal studies beyond 100 m depth
Gravity profiling to detect large density contrasts in the bedrock
Seismic refraction using hammer sources for deep oil exploration
questions.solution: GPR: electromagnetic waves. Utility detection, void mapping, archaeology.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Seismic refraction — critical refraction:
options: Direct arrival that travels entirely within the surface layer after reflection at the boundary
Wave reflected from the interface returned to the surface at an angle equal to the incident angle
Surface wave travelling along the ground with velocity independent of layer properties
Head wave at critical angle (sin i_c = V₁/V₂). Refractor velocity V₂ from intercept time
questions.solution: Refraction: first arrivals. Crossover distance. Layer thickness: h = (x_c/2)√((V₂-V₁)/(V₂+V₁)).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Groundwater occurrence in hard rock terrains is primarily controlled by:
options: Water in hard rocks occurs only within primary intergranular pores between mineral grains
Fracture-controlled. Weathered zone (shallow) + fractured zone (deeper). Yield variable
The rock mass behaves as a porous medium with a uniform and very high storage capacity
Yield is uniform everywhere and entirely independent of the fracture network
questions.solution: Hard rock: only secondary porosity. Fracture zones, lineaments. High-yield wells along major fractures.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Goldschmidt's geochemical classification of elements groups Cu, Pb and Zn predominantly into which class?
options: Siderophile (Fe-loving, concentrated in the metallic core)
questions.solution: Goldschmidt's classes: lithophile (Si, Al, K), siderophile (Fe, Ni, Au), chalcophile (Cu, Pb, Zn, S) and atmophile (N, noble gases). Chalcophiles concentrate in sulfide phases.
